text:
sam: noticed a perf regression on nightly e2e for kv-cache-heavy traffic. tail latency spikes ~3x after the driver bump. ran an nsys timeline and the kernel selection looks weird — lots of tiny generic_gemm launches instead of the fused kernels we used to see.

anita: which nsys / driver exact versions? can you paste the capture command and the offending timeline snippet? :mag:

sam: nsys 2024.4, driver 535.86.10, cuda 12.2. capture command: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=cuda,nvtx --force-overwrite 
  python perf_test_runner.py --workload kvcache_hotpath
```
Here is the top timeline bit (snip):
```
[CUcontext 0x7fdd] kernel generic_gemm_1 size=128x128 time=220us
[CUcontext 0x7fdd] kernel generic_gemm_1 size=128x128 time=210us
[CUcontext 0x7fdd] memcpy H2D 5us
[CUcontext 0x7fdd] kernel generic_gemm_2 size=64x64 time=190us
[... many short kernel launches ...]
KV cache hit ratio looks same but per-token time up.
```

ben: we saw something similar after 535.x updates — nvprof/nsys stopped showing the optimized fused kernels in traces, instead showing many smaller kernels. there was a CUPTI symbol mismatch in 2024.3/4 with 535.* drivers. error shows up intermittently. did the nsys log have any CUPTI errors?

sam: yes, intermittent lines in the nsys stderr: 
```
CUPTI ERROR: cuptiActivityEnable returned 0x7fffffff (CUPTI_ERROR_UNKNOWN)
CUPTI WARNING: activity buffer overflow
```

carol: that exact string rang a bell. rootless containers + newer drivers -> CUPTI sometimes fails to attach and nsys falls back to lower-fidelity sampling which can distort kernel aggregation, making kernels appear split. are you running this in a k8s job or local container?

sam: k8s (dedicated inference node, container runtime rootless). nodes have /dev/nvidia* exposed and driver is system-level. trace job runs as non-root service account.

ben: workaround we used: run nsys outside the container on the host (nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx) or give the pod CAP_SYS_ADMIN and mount /sys/kernel/debug to allow CUPTI to set breakpoints. not ideal for CI. also downgrading nsys to 2023.12 worked for us.

dave: i repro'd in a VM (non-root user) — nsys attaches but CUPTI claims buffer overflow then you get lots of tiny kernel entries. perf and nvprof agree that the kernels are still fused on device, so it's a tooling view problem, not the runtime changing kernel selection. here's perf record top lines: 
```
(vmlinux)   34.5%  python       [kernel.kallsyms]  <generic_cuda_dispatch>
(nv)       45.1%  python       [cuda kernel]        fused_matmul_kernel
```
so device saw fused_matmul_kernel; nsys showed generic_gemm_x.

carol: that aligns with a CUPTI/channel attribution bug. we also saw it affect batching heuristics analysis because the profiler counts many short kernels and our batching logic assumed longer contiguous kernels to allow continuous batching. testing note: don't trust the nsys kernel name aggregation if CUPTI errors present.

sam: ok — so next steps: try host-run capture for ground truth, and re-run nsys with --capture-range=cpuopri and --force-overwrite? any flags that helped you stabilize the capture?

ben: use `NSYS_NVTX_SAMPLING=1` + `--trace=cuda,nvtx,cudatrace` helped in one case. also `--cudatrace-keep-alive` (not documented?) was helpful when CUPTI detach raced. if host-run isn't possible, downgrade to nsys 2023.12 or pin driver to known-good 525.x in CI nodes.

carol: another safe option: use CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONCURRENT_KERNEL with cupti callbacks in a lightweight harness (small C wrapper) to validate kernel names before trusting nsys post-processed names. painful but quick to verify.

sam: can someone try host capture on staging node and attach the .qdrep? i'm going to revert the driver on a single node to see if latency goes back down.

infra-bot: rollback job queued: rollback-driver-535.86.10 -> 525.85.05 on node inference-04 — ETA ~12m :gear:

ben: if rollback fixes it we'll pin driver in autoscaler image selection. also add an integration job: host-nsys-smoke that runs nightly as root to catch CUPTI/display regressions early. :thumbsup:

carol: adding a note to the perf playbook: when you see many short kernels in nsys but perf shows fused ones, suspect CUPTI/driver tooling mismatch. include command snippet to collect host trace and perf as baseline.

sam: thanks all — I'll post qdrep + perf artifacts to the thread when available. :rocket:
